sections: Two weeks before

Check that your passport and visa are in order, since many sign-ups ask for them. Tell your bank you are travelling and ask about foreign fees, daily limits and how to lock a lost card. Decide which payment options you want to use, and read the current terms of each from the provider's own pages.
Cards

Take two cards from different accounts if you can. Keep them in different bags. Check that each works abroad, and note the bank's international phone number. Make sure contactless and PIN features are active. Ask whether a card has a fee for foreign purchases or ATM withdrawals, and how much it is.
Wallets and apps

If you plan to use a wallet for QR payments, download it from the official store and sign up before you leave. Identity checks can take time, and mobile data may be patchy on arrival. Test the login at home, and note how to reach support. Keep screenshots of confirmation emails.
Phone and data

Check how you will get mobile data in India, whether through roaming, an eSIM or a local SIM. Many payment and ride apps need a stable connection and a code sent to your phone. Carry a power bank. A dead phone makes every other plan harder.
A little cash

Bring a small amount of rupees, or plan to get some at the airport or from an ATM soon after landing. Small notes are most useful for tea, snacks, tips and rides. Check the exchange rate and fees before you change money, and keep the receipt.
Save the important details

Keep an offline note with your hotel address and phone number, your bank's international numbers, your insurance policy number and your passport details. Keep a second copy with a trusted person at home. If you lose your phone, that note could be what gets you going again.
On arrival

Do not rush. Pick a safe airport counter or an ATM inside the terminal, get enough for the first day and check your phone is working. Then head to your hotel and settle in. Ask your hotel what is easy to pay by card and what is better in cash nearby.
A simple order of tasks

Start with the slow items: identity checks and anything that needs a document. Then set up cards and alerts. Then download apps and test logins. Last, pack the physical items: cards, a little cash, a power bank and your offline notes. Ticking these off over a week is much calmer than doing them the night before the flight.
Common slips to avoid

Travellers often forget to tell their bank, keep both cards in the same wallet, leave their phone number unlinked to an account or arrive with no small notes. Each is easy to fix at home and annoying to fix abroad. Read your list one more time at the airport, before you board.
Why it pays to be early

Many sign-ups ask for photos, documents and a code sent to your phone. If you try this in an arrivals hall with weak signal, it becomes stressful. Done at home, with good Wi-Fi and time to read, it is easy. Treat it as part of packing, like choosing shoes.
A ZikPe note

Check ZikPe's official product information, eligibility and current terms before relying on it for a trip. Keep another payment method available and confirm that the merchant accepts the method you intend to use.
ZikPe's published starting point: passport and visa

ZikPe's official visitor guide says to download the app and sign up with passport and visa details, without an Indian bank account. Start from the official website's app links rather than an advertisement or a similarly named app. Those published requirements do not establish eligibility for every nationality, age or visa type. Confirm the requirements shown for your own case before relying on the wallet for arrival-day spending.
A published journey is not a timed app test

The official guide outlines signup, international-card top-up and QR payment. This article has not tested the current app screens and does not promise a two-minute activation, instant KYC approval or a particular PIN sequence. Follow the actual in-app checks and do not upload identity documents to a support chat or third-party link simply because it claims to accelerate verification. Keep another payment method until activation and a small payment are confirmed.
Check the top-up preview before loading

The official guide names international Visa and Mastercard for top-up and says the app shows the rupee amount, including fees, before confirmation. Review that amount for the exact card and transaction. A supported network does not guarantee every issuer will authorise a load, and the card issuer may add its own charges. Avoid loading the whole trip budget before you understand the actual wallet limits and how unused money is returned.
Why a wallet at all

A prepaid wallet lets you load money once and pay at many shops by scanning QR codes. For a visitor without an Indian bank account, it can be a way to use the same QR system that locals use. It is optional. Many trips run well on a card and some cash.
Check who can sign up

Providers set their own rules on which passports, countries and visa types they accept. They may also ask for photo identity checks, which take time. Read this section of the provider's page first, because it decides whether the rest matters to you. The National Payments Corporation of India has described UPI One World as a wallet for inbound travellers. Eligibility has changed over time, so check current terms.
Look at the money in and out

Find out how you can load the wallet, whether by card or bank transfer, and in which currency. Check whether there are loading fees, minimum or maximum amounts and an expiry date on the balance. Then find out how to get unused money back. A clear refund route is a good sign.
Look at where it works

A wallet is useful only if shops accept it. Most small merchants who show a UPI QR code are meant to accept payments from compatible wallets, but individual shops can vary. Ask your hotel which places nearby take QR payments and which prefer cash.
Look at support and safety

Check that the app comes from an official store and that there is a clear way to contact support. Be wary of any provider that asks you to pay a fee through a personal account or share a one-time code. Keep your passcode private and review the transaction list each evening.
Compare with the alternatives

A forex card, a regular card and cash each have strengths. Compare the real costs and the convenience, not just the headline. For many visitors a mix is best. Write down the three or four things that matter most to you, such as speed, cost and ease of refund, and compare against those.
Do a test run

Once set up, make one small purchase, such as a tea, to see how it works. Check the confirmation and the balance. If anything looks odd, contact support before relying on it. A small test is far better than a first payment at a busy counter.
Questions worth writing down

Before you sign up, write a short list: Is my passport accepted? How long does verification take? What does it cost to load and to withdraw? What is the daily limit? How do I reach a person if something fails? Having your own list means you compare providers on the same terms instead of on marketing. Keep the answers in a note. If a provider's page does not answer a question, email support and wait for a clear reply before you put money in.
What a good experience looks like

A good wallet feels plain. The sign-up steps make sense, the fees are written clearly, the balance updates quickly and the confirmation of each payment is easy to read. You never feel rushed or pushed into paying for extras. If any step feels confusing or pushy, trust that feeling and consider another option. There is no prize for committing early.
A ZikPe note

Check ZikPe's official product information, eligibility and current terms before relying on it for a trip. Keep another payment method available and confirm that the merchant accepts the method you intend to use.
ZikPe's published fees: distinguish the load from payment

ZikPe's terms, with the fees section effective from 12 October 2026, state a top-up fee of 2.5% of the amount loaded. They state no fee for opening, monthly or inactivity maintenance, or wallet closure. The terms also warn that a card issuer can separately charge for foreign transactions or currency conversion. Read the actual rupee-credit preview before confirming a load. Do not interpret no maintenance fee as no cost of using the service.
Rewards are plan-dependent Zik Coins

The same terms describe eligible outgoing wallet UPI payments earning Zik Coins at Passport 0%, Globe 2% or Infinity 5%, with the applicable plan shown in the app. That is not an unconditional 5% cash return on every transaction. Loads, fees, refunds, failed or reversed transactions do not earn those rewards, and the terms say Zik Coins have no cash value except where the app expressly allows otherwise. Compare the cost and usefulness of a plan before treating rewards as savings.
Ask about the unresolved limits

The public pages checked for this article do not provide a complete country-by-country eligibility list or every wallet and transaction limit. Confirm those details for your account instead of importing another provider's rules. The official visitor guide describes QR payments; that alone is not evidence that every Amazon or Uber checkout flow supports this wallet. A particular online transaction needs its own compatibility check.

sections: The idea in one line

A UPI-linked wallet holds money you have loaded in advance. When you scan a shop's QR code, the app takes the amount from that balance and sends it to the shop. You do not need cash, and you do not hand a card to anyone. It is the same QR system many people in India use, with a prepaid balance behind it.
Step one: sign up

You download the provider's app from an official store and create an account. Providers usually ask for identity details, often a passport and visa for visitors, and sometimes a photo. This step can take a little while, so do it before you travel if you can. Read the terms on who can sign up, since rules differ between providers.
Step two: load money

You add money by a method the provider accepts, such as a card or a bank transfer. Check the fees, the minimum and maximum amounts and whether the balance expires. Load only what you expect to spend. Many travellers start with a modest amount and top up later.
Step three: scan and pay

At a shop, open the app and scan the printed QR code. The screen shows the shop's name. Check it, type the amount, confirm with your passcode and wait for a confirmation. The shopkeeper usually gets a message or a spoken alert. Keep your screen on until you see the confirmation.
Step four: keep an eye on things

The app lists every payment. Look at it each evening, so you notice any mistake early. If a payment fails but the money leaves your balance, keep a screenshot and contact the provider's support. Most failed payments are reversed, but it can take a little time.
What it cannot do

A wallet is meant for paying merchants. It is not a bank account, it does not earn interest and some shops may not accept it. Cash or a card still matter in smaller places, so carry a backup. Knowing the limits keeps your plan realistic.
Getting unused money back

The National Payments Corporation of India says UPI One World allows unused balance to be transferred back to the original payment source. Other providers have their own rules and timelines. Check how and when you can withdraw before you load much money, and keep your receipts.
Staying safe

Use only official apps, keep your passcode private and never share one-time codes. Ignore messages that ask you to pay a fee to unlock a wallet or claim a refund. Only scan QR codes at a counter you can see. If something feels wrong, stop and contact the provider through its official page.
A sample first day

You wake up, check your balance and head out. A morning chai is paid by scanning the stall's code. A taxi ride is cash, lunch is a card and an afternoon snack is another scan. By evening, you review the list in your app and top up if needed. It feels more natural by the second day.
Questions to ask your provider

How long does verification take? What are the limits? What happens if a payment fails? How do I contact support from abroad? How and when can I get unused money back? Write the answers in a note so you can find them quickly later.
Common mistakes

Visitors sometimes load too much, forget their passcode, scan a code that is not at a counter or skip the confirmation screen. Each is easy to avoid with a small routine. Slow down for a second at every payment.
A ZikPe note

Check ZikPe's official product information, eligibility and current terms before relying on it for a trip. Keep another payment method available and confirm that the merchant accepts the method you intend to use.
ZikPe's published flow, without invented screens

For ZikPe specifically, the official guide describes signup using passport and visa, a top-up using an international Visa or Mastercard, a rupee-and-fee preview, then QR payment. This is a summary of the provider's published process, not a hands-on certification of the current interface. Check the merchant name and amount before approving a payment, and keep a backup for network, verification or acceptance problems.
Transaction refunds and unused balance are different

ZikPe's refund policy discusses failed or returned transactions separately from account deactivation. It says card-statement processing may take four to seven business days and also includes restrictions on the use or withdrawal of refund amounts. Those statements should not be turned into a blanket promise that every merchant refund returns instantly to your card. Keep the transaction reference and ask official support which route applies to the actual case.
Deactivation and deletion are not the same request

The refund policy gives Profile > Settings > Deactivate Account as the deactivation route, states processing within twenty-four to forty-eight hours and says remaining balances go to original source accounts after pending transactions are completed. The separate account-deletion page describes deletion or anonymisation within thirty days after verification, with some KYC and transaction records retained under law. Confirm the treatment and timing of your balance before leaving India. Neither deletion nor deactivation should be used as a guessed shortcut around an unresolved refund.
Use the provider's current support channel

The published terms give support@zikpe.com for service grievances and account closure requests. Use the address reached through the official site, keep the issue and transaction details concise, and never share an OTP or PIN. A customer-service address does not establish a guaranteed response time or outcome. If the published refund wording seems inconsistent for your case, get an account-specific explanation before relying on a withdrawal date.
